rationale: Both designs are competent and agree on the essentials: ULIDs, a POST cancel sub-resource instead of DELETE, an Idempotency-Key header, a bounded queue with 429 and Retry-After, SSE plus polling, and URI versioning with Sunset headers. B is more rigorous and more operationally aware. It makes 'cancelling' an observable state and verifies VRAM is released before admitting the next job, the real failure mode on a single GPU. It returns 409 when an idempotency key is replayed with a different body, which catches a common client bug, and replays the stored response verbatim. It adds ETag/304 polling, cursor-resumable SSE, signed artifact URLs to keep the control plane thin, opt-in best-effort webhooks, request-ID correlation, and a forward-compatibility rule for unknown status values. It also includes a concrete job object and rejects MIG sharing while reserving a field for it. A has small inconsistencies. Its cancel example shows a queued job still in 'queued' although it says queued jobs cancel immediately. Its state machine omits the running-to-timed_out transition despite a deadline field. And it implies DELETE is not idempotent, when HTTP defines DELETE as idempotent. A's 201-versus-202 argument and cancel_requested flag are good, but B is the stronger design overall.
